answer: Because the cipher lockup is enforced by the canyon escrow, the river audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. The bond is locked for 47 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Running a large army of identities therefore freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants forfeit once per identity. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
